how.title: How article improvements work
how.intro: We review how the articles on your website perform in Google Search. When the data shows a clear opportunity to rank better, we rewrite that article, changing only the parts that need it.
steps: Scan performance
Through Google Search Console we track clicks, impressions, click-through rate and rankings for every article.
Rewrite with purpose
On each improvement day we rewrite the article with the clearest opportunity. It's prepared the day before, so it's ready for review on the day.
You stay in control
Approve or reject each change one by one. Nothing goes live until you approve, unless auto-approve is on. Flagged rewrites always wait for your review.
Measure the impact
Two weeks after an improvement goes live, we compare its clicks and impressions with the two weeks before.
how.eligibility: Articles that already perform well are left alone. To qualify, a page needs at least 90 days in Google Search and real search demand. Pages improved in the last 6 months, or rejected in the last 4 weeks, are skipped. When several pages qualify, the one with the most impressions goes first.
how.scope: Articles written here, on any publishing platform, and every other post on your WordPress site once WordPress is connected. In those posts, images, videos, tables, FAQ and other blocks stay exactly as they are, sections that aren't improved aren't touched, and WordPress keeps the previous version in the post's revisions. Posts built with a page builder such as Elementor or Divi are skipped.

items: Open the Lovable project you want the blog on.

Let Lovable build. It asks for the key in the next step.

items: Wait for Lovable to ask for {secret}.

steps: Create an app
In the Shopify Dev Dashboard, click Create app, start from the Dev Dashboard, give it any name and create it.
Give it product access
Under API access, select the scopes read_products and read_inventory, then click Release.
Install it on your store
On the app's Overview page, click Install app and choose your store.
Copy the credentials
Open the app's Settings and copy the Client ID and Client secret.

steps: Open the REST API settings
In WordPress, go to WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API and click Add key.
Create a Read key
Give it a description, keep your administrator account as the user and set Permissions to Read.
Copy the key and secret
Click Generate API key and copy the Consumer key (ck_…) and Consumer secret (cs_…). WooCommerce shows them only once.

credits.title: Backlink exchange explained
steps: Starting credits
Every site starts with 100 credits, so it can receive backlinks right away.
Earn credits
When one of your articles gives a live backlink, you earn credits equal to your domain rating, up to 20 per backlink (up to 10 for websites on a platform address such as yourstore.myshopify.com).
Spend credits

When you receive a backlink, you spend credits equal to the giving site's domain rating. A link from a stronger site costs more than one of yours earns, so your balance can dip below zero for a while.
Self-balancing
While your balance is below zero, incoming backlinks pause. Your new articles keep giving links, which brings it back up automatically.
credits.placement: Links are added inside new articles published by sites in the network, only where the linked page genuinely helps the reader. They are normal (dofollow) links in the text, and they count once we've seen them live on the page.
